detail: Landing B (10-14/15) measured that LOCAL-izing each generic's implementation closure to a strict universal seal needs either copies of ~361 shared library books (refused: a twin forest, collides on FN-RECORD-INTERNALS) or an in-place public/internal split of the shared libraries. Measurement protocol (main 10-14, binding for this item): the export set is the fixpoint of every edge ACL2 imposes when an UNCHANGED retained event is replayed in pass 2 with its target LOCAL (kinds so far: event incl. owning source form, logical support, constraint container, rule-class prerequisites), each kind named from ACL2 semantics with one ground refusal witness, joining by measurement; STOP line: an edge kind whose theorem-rule runes exceed 1% of the generic's U theorem-rule runes beyond those already accepted. Retirement targets: stobj/abstract-stobj declarations (companion + support debt). Evidence: lane one-world-b build/b-runs (B-S-*.txt, B-S-DSTAR/TSTAR/final reports, edge witnesses).
notes: 10-15 01:51 2026-10-15 A29: deleting the X/X4/X5 snapshot exports (lane one-world-b cc16d64da, certify run-20261015T051200Z-5a02) fixed the three old reds at their pair (admission-memory, checkpoint-codec, checkpoint-payloads-extent) but exposed EIGHT more root reds (345 books failed in cascade): paged-checkpoint-stage (call depth, FN-PCK-X-PUT-ROW), recovery-profile-buffer (call depth, FN-RPF-PREFIX-FROM), payload-lz-record (guard FN-LZR-EXPAND), store-log-route (FN-OLR-VERDICT-UNDER-THE-LINK), store-reclaim-holders (guard FN-RCL-SUMMARY-IN), topic-history-store-invariants (FN-STI-CURRENT-RECORDS-TOPIC-OK), tests served-catalog-join (call depth), heap-figure (timeout). Machinery kept (reverted 6d0db4244) per main's ruling C(2); its deletion belongs to this item. The three pair repairs are recorded in cc16d64da for reuse.
title: seal each generic's exported vocabulary: the leak is shared-library vocabulary, not generic-private; a vocabulary refactor (public/internal split of shared libraries and the stobj declarations), not a landing
